prompt: Implement bubble sort so it sorts the given array IN PLACE (ascending) and returns the very same array object it was given.
explanation: Bubble sort compares each pair of neighbors and swaps them when they are out of order; after each full sweep the largest remaining value has 'bubbled' to the end, so the sweep can stop one position earlier each time. The swapped flag lets an already-sorted array finish after a single sweep. Sorting IN PLACE means mutating the array you were handed and returning that same reference, not a copy.
hints: Swapping two array slots needs a temp variable: temp = a[i]; a[i] = a[i+1]; a[i+1] = temp;
Repeat sweeps until a whole sweep performs zero swaps -- track that with a boolean flag.
Return a itself at the end. The test checks result == input, so a new array will fail.
